title: Wave-direction interactions gave no clear six-hour Monterey forecast gain in nine retained years within 2010-2023
abstract: We tested whether Bodega Bay wave-direction interactions improve six-hour Monterey mean-wave-height forecasts beyond additive direction controls and partner wave history. Annual fits used only earlier records from 2000 onward. There were 8,106 retained cases in nine years within 2010-2023. The main interaction MSE reduction was 0.69%, with a conditional 95% three-year calendar-block interval of -0.38% to 1.69%. A penalty-10 check gave a positive interval, so the result depends on the model. Partner wave-height terms gave a larger gain for northern-source than southern-source cases: 42.84% versus 22.33%, a 20.51-point difference [7.04, 37.90]. This sector difference does not identify wave travel as a cause. The source snapshot overlaps an earlier campaign study. Missing direction data, one station pair, revised archives and fixed-fit resampling limit use. Code, aggregate scores, model parameters, exact source hashes, an independent audit, a figure and retrieval instructions are included. Source time series and record-level derivatives stay external.

display.caption: Partner wave-height gain by source-direction half and added direction-interaction gain by model setting. Bars show conditional 95% three-year calendar-block intervals for retained 2010-2023 cases.
